answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule. Each identity's actions are scored per epoch against a slow-moving baseline; the allowed delta between current and prior behaviour shrinks as history lengthens. A sustained drift beyond that delta triggers a terrace effect: privileges taper stepwise until fresh proof-of-work accrues. The baseline acts as an anchor that impersonators cannot cheaply fake. Attacker cost: maintaining many identities requires genuine behavioural continuity across epochs, multiplying effort and time per fake identity.
